title: Inside GitHub’s new Git storage architecture
content: GitHub announced “Project Rubicon,” a new Git storage architecture supporting thousands of writes per second. By decoupling storage from compute, it uses Azure Blob Storage for immutable data and a “Ref-CAS” service for reference updates. Virtual replicas handle requests, while separate compaction nodes maintain performance. This design minimizes coordination, ensuring low latency and scalability for high-volume repositories. The architecture currently serves in a private preview, with broader rollout planned for next year to support agentic development.

title: Accessibility statements now have a home on GitHub
content: GitHub now recognizes an `ACCESSIBILITY.md` file in repositories, providing a standardized location for documenting accessibility goals, supported environments, and barrier reporting processes. This file improves the discoverability of accessibility information alongside existing community guidelines. The platform encourages maintainers to publish accurate, maintainable statements that outline contributor expectations, known limitations, and response workflows. By centralizing this information, GitHub aims to normalize accessibility practices across open-source projects, helping users and contributors understand project commitments and effectively report issues.
